schemes.label: Capacity Market
schemes.attribution_note: Only the part of the Capacity Market that net zero caused is counted. Any power system needs backup, so each year's levy is reduced by what the same system without net-zero policy would have paid at that year's capacity price for its own backup; the remainder is counted. Shares for 2016-2025 come from a model of that system; later years use the 2025 share (27.7%) until the model covers them. The figure is a floor: a 550 g/kWh emissions limit has kept about 11 GW of coal out of the four-year-ahead auctions since 2021, and capacity prices rose after it; no published source measures how much of that rise net zero caused, so none of it is counted.
schemes.source: LCCC data portal, capacity market payments

schemes.label: Renewables Obligation
schemes.source: Ofgem Renewables Obligation Annual Reports. 2024 (SY23): Annual Report 2024-25 headline scheme value (PDF, RO_24-25_SY23_Annual_Report, Mar 2026). 2010-2023 (SY9-SY22): scheme value = total ROCs presented x notional worth of a ROC, Figure A4.1 of the SY22 Annual Report (2023-24, PDF, Mar 2025), cross-checked against headline values stated in the SY22/SY23 report text (SY1 GBP 0.25bn, SY18 GBP 6.31bn, SY19 GBP 5.73bn, SY22 GBP 6.75bn, SY23 GBP 7.70bn). 2002-2009 (SY1-SY8): ROCs presented x worth of a ROC from the compliance tables of Ofgem's second annual report (2003-04, Feb 2005), the RO Annual Report 2004-2005 (Feb 2006), the RO Annual Report 2008-09 (Feb 2010) and the RO Annual Report 2010-11 (Mar 2012).

schemes.label: Feed-in Tariffs
schemes.source: Ofgem Feed-in Tariffs Annual Report Scheme Year 15 (April 2024 to March 2025), Figure 3.3 "FIT scheme value, SY1-15" (PDF, feed_in_tariff_annual_report_sy15, Dec 2025). The report states the series grew every year from SY1 to SY11 (GBP 1,764m), fell for the first time in SY12 (GBP 1,575m), peaked at GBP 1,858m in SY14, and was GBP 1,844m in SY15, which fixes the year order of the charted values.

schemes.label: Climate Change Levy on electricity (to July 2015) + Carbon Price Support
schemes.attribution_note: Two parts. (1) The Climate Change Levy on electricity, counted only up to 31 July 2015, while renewable electricity was exempt (it carried Levy Exemption Certificates) and the levy therefore fell on fossil and nuclear power alone; from 1 August 2015 renewable electricity paid it too (Finance (No. 2) Act 2015 s.49), so later receipts are not counted. 2015 counts 7/12 of the year: HMRC publishes no monthly electricity receipts, and its monthly declarations are booked by quarter. (2) Carbon Price Support, counted in full: a tax only fossil-fuelled generators pay. Gas/solid-fuel main-rate CCL is excluded throughout.
schemes.source: HMRC Environmental Taxes Bulletin (formerly Climate Change Levy and Carbon Price Floor Bulletin), March 2026 edition, tables ODS (2026_March_env_tabs_test.ods), Table 1b "CCL and CPF receipts and clearances data by calendar year": electricity main-rate declared liabilities (the only commodity split HMRC publishes) and estimated CPF receipts (Carbon Price Support, which applies solely to fossil fuels used for electricity generation). The two parts are stored separately below (components) and summed into annual; each part rounded down to the nearest GBP 0.1m. Exemption end: Finance (No. 2) Act 2015 s.49, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2015/33/section/49/enacted , which inserted "(za) it is generated before 1 August 2015" into the renewable exemption, FA 2000 Sch 6 para 19(3).

schemes.label: Emissions trading (power-sector share of UK auction revenue)
schemes.attribution_note: Power-sector share of AUCTIONED allowance revenue only; free allocation excluded. Share taken as electricity generation's share of total verified covered emissions - a lower bound, since power receives no free allocation and so buys a larger share of auctioned allowances than its emissions share.
schemes.source: Auction revenue: 2012-2018 calendar-year sums of UK EUA auction results from the European Commission's UK Phase III Auction Platform Reports nos. 57 and 58 (ICE Futures Europe auctions on behalf of BEIS/DECC), converted from EUR at Bank of England annual average rates; 2019-2020 "EU ETS auction income" from the BEIS Annual Report and Accounts 2020-21 Trust Statement (FY2019-20 GBP 201.4m, FY2020-21 GBP 2,213.1m); 2021-2023 "UK ETS auction income" from the BEIS/DESNZ Annual Report and Accounts Trust Statements (FY2021-22 GBP 5,753,639k, FY2022-23 GBP 6,048,951k, FY2023-24 GBP 3,407,068k), attributed to the calendar year in which the financial year starts. 2024 uses the PUBLISHED CALENDAR-YEAR total instead - see calendar_year_revenue below. Power-sector share: from published UK ETS verified emissions (electricity generation / total covered); 2009-2020 a flat 0.5 estimate. See emissions_vintage below for the figures and their editions.

schemes.label: Extra grid costs of net zero (TNUoS)
schemes.attribution_note: Raw totals stored; attribution happens in the money model. Each year counts the cost above what the grid would have cost without net zero; a year below it counts negative, and only the 2002-to-date total is floored at zero (netted over the whole period, 14 Oct 2026). These are costs of net zero, not payments to generators. That cost, year by year, comes from the gas-counterfactual model (release v4-s35; GBP 2.44bn in 2025): the 2002-05 grid cost carried forward by the index the regulator used (RPI to 2020/21, then CPIH), plus the whole of the regulator's allowance for renewing the ageing grid above its 2002-05 level, as the regulator pays it (a return on, and depreciation of, the asset value). Years after 2025, the model's last year, carry the 2025 figure forward with CPIH.
schemes.source: Every year from a primary document (v4-s35, T9, 14 Oct 2026). FY2001/02-2005/06: GB transmission owners' allowed revenues, NGC (Ofgem Sep 2000 final proposals Table A6.2) + SP Transmission and SHETL (Ofgem BETTA proposals Jul 2004 Tables 1-2; FY2005/06 from the Dec 2004 final proposals Table 2.3), restated to money of the year by RPI (no GB TNUoS existed before BETTA, April 2005). FY2006/07: Ofgem TPCR4 final proposals Dec 2006 Table 2.1. FY2007/08-2009/10: Ofgem Transmission Annual Reports, "Total Actual Revenue" (NGET, including income collected for the Scottish TOs). FY2010/11-2012/13: National Grid TNUoS statement 2012/13 "Total TNUoS revenue". FY2013/14 onwards: National Grid / NESO TNUoS charging statements and Final TNUoS Tariffs (2021/22 £3,318m; 2023/24 £4,416.4m; 2024/25 MAR total £4,188.5m). FY2013/14-2020/21 were taken until 14 Oct 2026 from David Turver's workbook compiling the same statements (a secondary source); they are now read from the statements themselves, which differ for 2013/14 (£2,153.0m, not £2,196.6m), 2014/15 (£2,477.3m, not £2,524.3m), 2018/19 (£2,670.0m, not £2,670.3m) and 2022/23 (£3,594.25m, not £3,594.0m). These are the gas-counterfactual engine's own series (gascf.grid.tnuos_fy; source ids in its data/raw/SOURCE_IDS.md). National Grid published the charging statements until NESO took over the role in Oct 2024; only the latest years are NESO documents.
schemes.raw_year_basis: calendar: 0.25 x FY(y-1) + 0.75 x FY(y) of the stored financial-year charges (CY2002 uses FY2001/02)

netting.rule: Netted over the whole period: each year's figure is the measured cost minus the no-net-zero cost and may be negative; only the line's 2002-to-date total is floored at zero (until 14 October 2026 each year was floored at zero).

schemes.counterfactual_source: gas-counterfactual engine v4-s35 (GO5: no-net-zero grid cost; generators' share included)
schemes.counterfactual_method: GO5 (spec §7.1, §7.3): G0 carried by the transmission price controls' own index (RPI to FY2020/21, then CPIH; RIIO-ET2 PCFH para 2.17; gascf.grid.control_index_fy), plus the grid renewal allowance R: the non-load-related allowance above the 2002-05 level, rolled into an indexed RAV, depreciated straight line over 45 years, earning the current control's real allowed return (RIIO-ET2 PCFH para 4.1). Central = the whole allowance (v4-s35, Richard); low/high are by NET-ZERO cost: low = central (R whole), high = R not counted. Generators' share included.
schemes.counterfactual_range_labels: low/high = the ends of NET ZERO's cost range: low_gbp holds the LARGER no-net-zero cost (smaller net-zero cost), high_gbp the smaller
schemes.counterfactual_carry_forward: For a calendar year after carry_forward.from (the engine's last modelled year), the no-net-zero cost is that year's figure carried by CPIH: value(y) = value(from) x CPIH(y) / CPIH(from). The Clock applies it with its own CPIH series (and the latest index for a year without one, including the run-rate), the same series it deflates every line with.

schemes.label: Constraint turn-up (paid to switch on)
schemes.attribution_note: Estimated cost of paying other stations to replace the wind energy switched off for network constraints: each half-hour's switched-off wind volume priced against that half-hour's accepted offers (Octopus Energy Wasted Wind method). Taken out of the balancing (BSUoS) uplift, never more than it, so no total changes.
schemes.source: Elexon Insights settlement stacks (bids and offers)

schemes.label: Extra balancing costs of net zero (BSUoS)
schemes.attribution_note: Raw totals stored; attribution happens in the money model. Each year counts the cost above what balancing would have cost without net zero, NET of wind constraint payments already counted in the direct layer; a year below it counts negative, and only the 2002-to-date total of the balancing line (this line plus constraint turn-up) is floored at zero (netted over the whole period, 14 Oct 2026). For the current, part year the no-net-zero cost is pro-rated to the days the data covers. These are costs of net zero, not payments to generators. That cost, year by year, comes from the gas-counterfactual model (release v4-s35; GBP 1.45bn in 2025): the 2002-05 balancing cost split into an energy part that follows the gas price and a services part that follows CPIH (energy share from NESO's 2018-19 outturn, a share of external cost, so applied to the external part of the 2002-05 cost only). Years after 2025, the model's last year, carry the 2025 figure forward with CPIH. The estimated cost of replacing switched-off wind (constraint turn-up) is then shown as its own line and taken out of this one.
schemes.source: Every year from a primary document (v4-s35, T9, 14 Oct 2026). FY2001/02-2004/05: NGET, SO incentive scheme note, Dec 2005 (incentivised balancing cost, E&W), grossed up to GB by demand and by the SO internal-cost ratio (Ofgem Transmission Annual Report 2008-09 Table 22). FY2005/06: NAO, Electricity Balancing Services (May 2014, HC 41) para 2.2, £642m. FY2006/07: National Grid 2010 Table 1 IBC x the same internal ratio (estimated). FY2007/08-2009/10: Ofgem Transmission Annual Reports, SO external + internal costs. FY2010/11: interpolated in real terms between its neighbours (estimated). FY2011/12-2015/16: National Grid Monthly Balancing Services Summary, March issues section 10.3 (external + internal). FY2016/17: NESO BSUoS half-hourly charge data. These are the gas-counterfactual engine's own series (gascf.balancing.bsuos_fy and baseline_fy; source ids in its data/raw/SOURCE_IDS.md). The NAO 2011-13 even split (£861.5m a year) is replaced by the MBSS figures.

netting.rule: Netted over the whole period: each year's figure is the measured cost minus the no-net-zero cost and may be negative; only the line's 2002-to-date total is floored at zero (until 14 October 2026 each year was floored at zero).

schemes.counterfactual_source: gas-counterfactual engine v4-s35 (GO4: no-net-zero balancing cost, BSUoS basis; generators' share included)
schemes.counterfactual_method: GO4 (spec §7.2): B0 (option 'ibc', CY2002-05 mean) split into an energy part carried by the gas price gas(y)/gas(2002-05) and a services part carried by CPIH; energy share = NESO 2025 Annual Balancing Costs workbook, FY2018/19 (central), a share of external cost, so applied to B0's external part B0/(1 + SO internal ratio) only (v4-s35); SO internal costs ride on CPIH. Generators' share included. Range, by NET-ZERO cost: low = the stacked option 'nao_2005|max' (the largest no-net-zero cost), high = 'ibc|min', each as one rule for every year (chosen on the 2002-2025 total), so an end can cross the central: the high end lies above the central no-net-zero cost in 2002, 2003, 2004, 2020.
schemes.counterfactual_range_labels: low/high = the ends of NET ZERO's cost range: low_gbp holds the LARGER no-net-zero cost (smaller net-zero cost), high_gbp the smaller
schemes.counterfactual_carry_forward: For a calendar year after carry_forward.from (the engine's last modelled year), the no-net-zero cost is that year's figure carried by CPIH: value(y) = value(from) x CPIH(y) / CPIH(from). The Clock applies it with its own CPIH series (and the latest index for a year without one, including the run-rate), the same series it deflates every line with.
